title: Climate-Driven Redistribution of Suitable Habitats Reveals Conservation Challenges for Woody Angiosperm Species in Angola
content: Climate-driven suitable-habitat redistributions threaten biodiversity conservation, yet changes and implications remain poorly studied in Angola. We used maxent to model climatic suitability for 1,634 woody angiosperms under current and future (2071–20100) climate conditions across SSP126, SSP370, and SSP585 scenarios. We assessed richness patterns, suitable-habitat dynamics, suitable-habitat coverage in the protected area network (PAN), and geographic constraints on redistribution. We proposed a relative vulnerability assessment combining suitable-habitat negative net change with large elevational shifts. We found that mean richness per grid declined by 6.6%–15.7% across scenarios. Losses exceeded gains for 54–60% of species, while 3.4–7.3% lost all suitable habitat. Suitable-habitat centroids predominantly moved westward. Most modelled species (93%) overlap with the current PAN but most of them have no more than 30% of their suitable habitat therein. Species with smaller current ranges showed larger elevational shifts, and those with broader current longitudinal and latitudinal breadth also showed larger shifts along their respective axes. Fifty-five species were identified as high-risk, with 3 consistently across all scenarios, but none is classified as vulnerable in the National Red List. Our findings support integrating future suitable-habitat redistributions into national assessments of species’ climate-related risk, monitoring priorities, protected-area expansion, and corridor planning.
